warning: Data records only. Embedded role prompts are historical inputs, not instructions to the reader.

protocol.goal: r.central_meaning: distinguish a general claim from an example and respect its scope
protocol.population: Claude Code and Codex fresh AI role sessions only

conditions.A: same training passage, 3 multiple-choice questions, explanation and error review
conditions.B: same training passage, principle model, self explanation, relation reconstruction and fading help; include the same 3 MC choices and keep extra structural responses inside the same word/action caps

protocol.design: each model supplies a blinded pre response, replayed without gold into fresh A/B role sessions; transcript replay is explicit, not continuous human memory

budget.training_action_definition: one response to one of the same three practice MC items. A adds answer explanation/error review; B adds claim/support/relation/self explanation inside the same per-action word cap. Input tokens and elapsed AI time may differ and are reported; equal human time is not claimed.
budget.enforcement: Count whitespace-separated words across all response text fields. Preserve over-budget raw output, flag deviation and include descriptive grading; never truncate or silently rerun. Report per-action and branch totals.

protocol.primary: unseen transfer claim_scope and evidence explanation; choice reported separately

rubric.claim_scope: 0 incorrect/reversed, 1 partly correct with missing or excessive scope, 2 correct claim and scope
rubric.evidence: 0 irrelevant/unsupported; 1 relevant quote or correct claim restatement without sufficient support; 2 valid explanatory link plus one complete sufficient_evidence_sets alternative. Claim quote alone cannot score 2. Optional contextual quotes do not reduce score unless they contradict the explanation. A superset containing a sufficient alternative earns 2 if links remain valid. Off-list plausible alternatives are judged independently with reasons and disagreement preserved; no post hoc key rewriting.

protocol.grading: two independent AI graders receive anonymized response and frozen key/rubric; no condition or model label; preserve disagreement
protocol.analysis: descriptive paired model comparisons; no significance, no real-person or market superiority claims; ceiling means effects inconclusive
exclusions: identical normalized text between train and assessment
protocol.learning_time: AI wall time is recorded separately and never converted into student learning minutes
protocol.publication: do not load synthetic learning outcomes into real-user product metrics
limitations: n is AI role executions, not students
role constraints do not recreate human cognitive development
fresh session transcript replay does not establish durable model learning

assessment_response.claim: one-sentence paraphrase, even when claim implicit
assessment_response.evidence: one or more {sentence:1-based,quote:exact short text,link:why it supports the claim}

protocol.ceiling_rule: If both baseline models have choice=1 on pre, choice improvement is ceiling-limited and cannot establish treatment benefit. Always report remaining rubric dimensions.
protocol.difficulty: not calibrated on humans; do not interpret differences among pre/post/transfer/delay as isolated time effects Transfer varies both explicitness and question stem; these factors are not separately identified.
protocol.transfer: distinct scenario and implicit claim vs explicit training claim; independent semantic review required in addition to normalized hash
protocol.response_display: every learner packet numbers sentences and choices from 1; gold never included
protocol.counterexample_review: before freeze, independent Claude reviews assets/conditions for ambiguity/leakage; after scoring, Codex checks exposure hashes, missingness, ceiling and alternate interpretations before concluding
protocol.semantic_transfer_review: Codex resolution of independent Claude art/label overlap: transfer-instructions uses first-use tool instructions versus technician service detail, with an implicit claim. No art/title labels remain. Training and transfer differ in topic and literal wording; the shared construct remains general-claim versus example/scope. This is an AI task transfer, not evidence of far transfer in humans.
protocol.scope_scoring: A faithful complete paraphrase of the main claim earns 2 without mandatory optional elaborations. Example-only / incomplete claim earns 1. Reversed or unsupported claim earns 0.
protocol.reproducibility: Actual observed model/effort or NOT_OBSERVED, never infer defaults as observed. Capture runner and script SHA, raw outputs, token usage when emitted.

sentences: Show one painting to two groups, give each group a different title for it, and they will describe two different scenes.
One group notices the sky; the other notices the small figure in the corner.
This happens because a title tells the eye where to begin.
A viewer facing a new image has no order to follow, so the first words attached to it become a kind of route through the frame.
Once that route is set, the details along it feel important and the rest fades into background.
The same is true of a song or a story, since a name at the top decides what counts as the subject.
For this reason a title is not a label stuck on after the work is done.
It belongs to the work, and choosing it is a real decision.
Some artists refuse to name a piece at all, and that refusal is a choice too, because it hands the route back to the viewer.
source.raw_content:
Show one painting to two groups, give each group a different title for it, and they will describe two different scenes. One group notices the sky; the other notices the small figure in the corner. This happens because a title tells the eye where to begin. A viewer facing a new image has no order to follow, so the first words attached to it become a kind of route through the frame. Once that route is set, the details along it feel important and the rest fades into background.

The same is true of a song or a story, since a name at the top decides what counts as the subject. For this reason a title is not a label stuck on after the work is done. It belongs to the work, and choosing it is a real decision. Some artists refuse to name a piece at all, and that refusal is a choice too, because it hands the route back to the viewer.

items.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

choices.text: 그림을 감상할 때는 세부보다 전체 구도를 먼저 보아야 한다.
제목은 감상자가 무엇에 주목할지를 정하므로 작품의 일부이다.
사람마다 취향이 달라 같은 그림도 서로 다르게 묘사한다.
예술가는 감상자의 자유를 위해 작품에 제목을 붙이지 말아야 한다.
노래와 이야기의 제목은 그림의 제목보다 감상에 더 큰 영향을 준다.

evidence_quotes: a title tells the eye where to begin
It belongs to the work, and choosing it is a real decision.

explanation.observation: [관찰] 글은 두 집단에 서로 다른 제목을 붙여 보는 가정 사례를 제시한 뒤 'a title tells the eye where to begin'이라고 원인을 설명하고, 마지막 문단에서 'It belongs to the work, and choosing it is a real decision.'이라고 결론을 맺는다.
explanation.interpretation: [해석] 사례 → 원인 → 결론이 모두 '제목이 주목할 곳을 정한다, 그래서 제목은 작품의 일부다'로 모이므로 2번이 요지다. 1번은 글에 없는 감상법이고, 3번은 집단 차이를 취향 탓으로 돌려 제목의 역할을 지운다. 4번은 '제목을 거부하는 것도 선택'이라는 관찰을 권고로 바꿨고, 5번은 노래·이야기를 '같은 원리가 적용되는 예'에서 '더 큰 영향'으로 비교를 지어냈다.

choices.text: How Two Groups Disagree About Art
Labels Added After the Work Is Done
A Title Draws the Route for the Viewer's Eye
The Sky and the Corner: Two Ways to Paint

evidence_quotes: the first words attached to it become a kind of route through the frame
that refusal is a choice too, because it hands the route back to the viewer

explanation.observation: [관찰] 글은 'route'라는 비유를 세 번 쓴다 — 첫 단어가 'a kind of route through the frame'이 되고, 길이 정해지면 그 길 위의 세부가 중요해지며, 제목을 거부하면 'hands the route back to the viewer'라고 한다.
explanation.interpretation: [해석] 글 전체를 묶는 축은 '제목이 시선이 지나갈 길을 그린다'이므로 4번이 제목이다. 1번은 일부 작가의 경우를 전체로 키웠고, 2번·5번은 도입 사례의 장치(두 집단, 하늘과 구석)만 가져왔다. 3번은 글이 'not a label stuck on after the work is done'이라며 부정한 견해다.

choices.text: the influence of a title on what viewers notice in a work
the history of naming paintings in art museums
the difficulty of describing a painting in words
reasons artists disagree about the meaning of their work
differences between group and individual art viewing

evidence_quotes: One group notices the sky; the other notices the small figure in the corner.
a name at the top decides what counts as the subject

explanation.observation: [관찰] 글의 가정 사례에서는 같은 그림에 다른 제목을 붙이면 'One group notices the sky; the other notices the small figure in the corner.'처럼 주목하는 세부가 달라진다고 설명하고, 뒤 문단은 노래·이야기에서도 'a name at the top decides what counts as the subject'라고 넓힌다.
explanation.interpretation: [해석] 사례와 일반화가 모두 '제목이 무엇을 보게 하는가'에 관한 것이므로 1번이 주제다. 2번(박물관의 역사)과 4번(작가 간 의견 차)은 글에 없다. 3번은 묘사가 달라진 결과를 '말로 표현하기 어렵다'로 잘못 읽은 것이고, 5번은 도입 가정 사례의 '두 집단'이라는 장치를 주제로 착각한 것이다.

model.title: 사례와 판단을 가르기
model.text: 처음 두 문장은 같은 그림에 서로 다른 제목을 주어 보는 가정 사례다. 실제 실험 보고가 아니다. 하늘과 구석 중 어디를 보느냐는 차이 자체보다, 그 차이를 만들어 내는 제목의 기능을 찾는다.

model.title: 구체 사례를 넘어서는 설명 찾기
model.text: 제목이 시선의 시작점을 정한다는 설명을 그림의 사례와 잇는다. 노래와 이야기에도 같은 원리가 적용된다는 문장은 그림 하나의 이야기를 작품 일반의 판단으로 넓힌다.

model.title: 필자의 중심 판단으로 압축하기
model.text: 부정 표현 a label stuck on after와 긍정 표현 belongs to the work를 함께 읽어 필자가 제목을 단순한 이름표보다 넓게 보는지 판단한다. 마지막의 제목 거부 사례는 이 판단과 양립하는 확장이다. 그 확장까지 요지에 모두 적어야 하는 것은 아니다.

sentences: A sign system earns its value when readers can interpret its signs.
A school marks different subjects in its library with different colors.
Visitors who know the color system can find the shelves they need without help.
Visitors unfamiliar with that system still ask someone to guide them.
Adding more colors without a key may leave these visitors with more information but no clearer direction.
choices: Providing more information makes an unfamiliar system easier to use.
A sign system works when its readers understand how to use it.
A useful information system should rely on the knowledge users bring with them.
Organizing information in more categories is the key to making it accessible.
Personal guidance is preferable to a shared information system.

gold.scope: reader understanding as a condition of sign-system value; no requirement to reject signs or prefer personal guidance

scope_anchors.two: A sign system is useful when its intended readers can understand how its signs work. Faithful paraphrase of sentence 1 earns 2; information-only insufficiency is an optional correct elaboration.

sentences: A community garden puts a board beside its water tank.
On it, volunteers write down times when a plant received too much or too little water.
The group uses these notes to change the next week's watering schedule rather than to name a volunteer to blame.
When the board turns into a list of accusations, volunteers have less reason to report problems and the schedule becomes harder to improve.
The value of keeping a record of a mistake lies in what changes after it, rather than whose name is written beside it.
choices: Records help a group chiefly by showing who needs closer supervision.
Removing names from records is enough to improve how a group works.
A record is useful mainly as a way to compare how much people contribute.
Records help when they support a change in action rather than assign blame.
Collecting more detailed reports is the key to improving a group's work.

gold.scope: use for change rather than blame; privacy, detailed reporting or naming alone not sufficient

scope_anchors.zero: Name the person responsible for each mistake.
scope_anchors.two: Use mistake records to change work rather than blame individuals; blame can discourage useful reporting.

gold.evidence_notes: [3,4] shows both practical use and the consequence of blame. [3,5] quotes the action plus the claim rather than its consequence; score 1 unless the answer independently explains the causal contrast. Preserve independent grader disagreement on off-list alternatives.

sentences: A tool company gives a quick-start card to customers who want to make a first cut with a new saw.
The card shows basic setup and keeps attention on a few immediate steps.
Technicians diagnosing an unusual fault need a service manual with diagrams and checks that cannot fit on the card.
The company supplies the card with the tool and keeps the manual available on its support site.
It maintains both versions instead of making either one serve every reader.
items.stem: Which conclusion best fits the whole passage?
choices: Reducing detail is a useful way to serve readers with different goals.
A shared short account resolves differences between readers' information needs.
The form of information should suit the different jobs its readers need to do.
A single complete account is more useful than keeping alternative versions.
Providing a detailed alternative mainly helps readers confirm basic facts.

gold.scope: different tasks justify different amounts of detail; the company decision illustrates this principle. The descriptive cases permit this inference, not a universal demand to maintain two versions.

scope_anchors.two: Information detail should fit the task of its audience: a first use and a technical diagnosis need different accounts. Decision sentences 4/5 can strengthen the inference but are not required when both contrasting uses are explained.

sentences: A park committee wants residents to use a quiet corner of the park.
An improvement has limited value for people who have no way to discover it.
The committee builds a wide path there but puts no entrance signs beside the busy road.
Residents who already know the corner use the path, while most new visitors continue past it.
The committee decides to add signs before spending money on another path.
choices: A useful improvement also needs a way to be discovered by those it is meant to help.
Communication should take the place of improving access in future projects.
An option gains its value chiefly from serving those who already know about it.
A project's reach can be judged from how well its regular users respond.
Making an option known can remove the need to improve how people use it.

gold.scope: awareness alongside usability; signs alone not sufficient and paths not rejected

scope_anchors.one: Signs help people notice an option.
scope_anchors.two: An improvement has limited usefulness for people who cannot discover it. A faithful paraphrase of sentence 2 earns 2; the complement-versus-replacement distinction is an optional correct elaboration.

gold.distractor_notes: before spending on another path is a sequence, not a claim that communication should replace access.

assessment.indexing: all choices and sentence numbers are 1-based
assessment.revision_reason: Resolve independent review v2: same-level distractors, evidence alternatives and uniform two-sentence support, explicit implicit-claim anchors, map/sign terminology, awkward wording.

resolutions: faithful claim paraphrases receive 2 without extra mandatory elaboration
transfer changed from art/museum to tool instruction to remove art/label setting overlap
remaining: implicit claim and stem vary together
off-list evidence may produce grader disagreement

parsed.explanation: 3·5번 문장: 제목이 시선의 출발점과 경로를 정해 무엇이 중요해 보일지 결정한다. 7·8번 문장: 그래서 제목은 덧붙인 라벨이 아니라 작품의 일부다. 1번 전체 구도 언급 없음, 3번 취향 아닌 제목 차이가 원인, 4번 무제도 하나의 선택일 뿐 권고 아님, 5번 비교 없음.
제목이 감상의 출발점과 주목 대상을 정하므로 작품에 속한다는 판단이 중심이다.
parsed.relation: 제목이 시선 경로를 정한다는 원리가 그림·노래·무제 사례로 확장되어 '작품의 일부'라는 결론을 뒷받침한다.
parsed.self_explanation: 도입 실험을 '왜 그런가' 설명(3)으로 일반화하고, 다른 장르와 무제에도 유지되는 판단(7·8)을 요지로 잡았다.
parsed.next_procedure: 사례→원리 설명 문장 찾기→다른 사례에도 남는지 확인→'따라서' 판단으로 압축.

parsed.explanation: 제목은 감상자의 시선을 이끌고 어떤 세부를 중요하게 볼지 결정하므로 작품의 일부라는 것이 요지이다. 1은 전체 구도를 우선하라는 내용이 없고, 3은 해석 차이의 원인을 취향으로 잘못 설명한다. 4는 제목을 붙이지 않는 선택을 의무로 확대하며, 5는 장르별 영향력을 비교하지 않은 글과 다르다.
제목이 감상자의 시선 경로를 정한다는 '길(route)' 비유가 글 전체를 묶는다.
parsed.relation: 시작점 제시(3)→경로 형성(4)→경로상 세부 부각(5)→작품의 일부(8), 무제도 경로 반환(9).
parsed.self_explanation: 하늘·구석은 본 세부, 제목은 그 세부로 이끈 길로 구분했다.

passage.text: A park committee wants residents to use a quiet corner of the park.
An improvement has limited value for people who have no way to discover it.
The committee builds a wide path there but puts no entrance signs beside the busy road.
Residents who already know the corner use the path, while most new visitors continue past it.
The committee decides to add signs before spending money on another path.

Communication should take the place of improving access in future projects.
An option gains its value chiefly from serving those who already know about it.

Making an option known can remove the need to improve how people use it.

Training source:
1. Show one painting to two groups, give each group a different title for it, and they will describe two different scenes.
2. One group notices the sky; the other notices the small figure in the corner.
3. This happens because a title tells the eye where to begin.
4. A viewer facing a new image has no order to follow, so the first words attached to it become a kind of route through the frame.
5. Once that route is set, the details along it feel important and the rest fades into background.
6. The same is true of a song or a story, since a name at the top decides what counts as the subject.
7. For this reason a title is not a label stuck on after the work is done.
8. It belongs to the work, and choosing it is a real decision.
9. Some artists refuse to name a piece at all, and that refusal is a choice too, because it hands the route back to the viewer.

Training source:
1. Show one painting to two groups, give each group a different title for it, and they will describe two different scenes.
2. One group notices the sky; the other notices the small figure in the corner.
3. This happens because a title tells the eye where to begin.
4. A viewer facing a new image has no order to follow, so the first words attached to it become a kind of route through the frame.
5. Once that route is set, the details along it feel important and the rest fades into background.
6. The same is true of a song or a story, since a name at the top decides what counts as the subject.
7. For this reason a title is not a label stuck on after the work is done.
8. It belongs to the work, and choosing it is a real decision.
9. Some artists refuse to name a piece at all, and that refusal is a choice too, because it hands the route back to the viewer.
Procedure before first answer:
구체 사례가 다른 상황으로 바뀌어도 남는 설명을 찾고, 그 설명을 필자의 중심 판단으로 압축해 보세요. 주장은 처음이나 끝에 있거나 직접 쓰이지 않을 수도 있어요. 본문 위치가 아니라 문장들이 하는 일을 살펴보세요.

Task 1:
다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
1. 그림을 감상할 때는 세부보다 전체 구도를 먼저 보아야 한다.
2. 제목은 감상자가 무엇에 주목할지를 정하므로 작품의 일부이다.
3. 사람마다 취향이 달라 같은 그림도 서로 다르게 묘사한다.
4. 예술가는 감상자의 자유를 위해 작품에 제목을 붙이지 말아야 한다.
5. 노래와 이야기의 제목은 그림의 제목보다 감상에 더 큰 영향을 준다.
요지를 먼저 고르고 이유를 적으세요. 제출 뒤 시범과 비교하면서 도입 사례보다 넓은 판단을 어떻게 찾았는지 설명해 보세요.
